newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy still awaits economic recovery - Confindustria.
newsitem.headline: Italy still awaits economic recovery - Confindustria.

text.p: The long-awaited economic upturn in Italy has still not appeared, the head of the industrialists' organisation, Confindustria said on Tuesday.
"We're now more than half way through the year and we're still waiting for clear signs of an economic recovery," Giorgio Fossa told a convention.

"We're not yet experiencing an (economic) pick-up. There has not been a turn around. We're still far from a true and proper recovery," he said, adding that Italy needed lower fiscal pressure and increase labour flexibility to boost the economy.
Italy's gross domestic product (GDP) fell by 0.4 percent, year-on-year, in the first quarter of 1997.

"The reason for the mediocre performance of the Italian economy is this: We have only straightened out (public) finances with larger taxes, bringing forward tax payments and delaying spending," Fossa said.
He said this had allowed Italy to bring its deficit to close to three percent of GDP. "But it has badly stalled the motor of the real economy," he added.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Monday he wanted to cut tax rates, but added that government accounts did not allow this at the moment. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
